paper_title: Transformations and Similar shapes Worksheet — Kalan
subject: Mathematics

questions.topic_aspect: Reflection in a given mirror line on a coordinate grid
questions.correct_answer: Image T' has vertices at (7,1), (7,3), (5,1) — the correct reflection of T in the line x = 2, with all vertices the same perpendicular distance from the mirror line as the corresponding original vertices, and correct (reversed) orientation.
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for at least one vertex of the image correctly reflected in the line x = 2 (i.e. correct perpendicular distance from mirror line, on opposite side), or for a fully correct triangle drawn in the wrong position/orientation showing correct method.
A1 for fully correct image T' drawn with vertices at (7,1), (7,3), (5,1), correctly labelled, with correct orientation (mirror image, not a translation or rotation).
questions.misconception_targeted: Reflecting in the wrong line or reversing orientation incorrectly

questions.topic_aspect: Rotation about a given centre by a stated angle and direction
questions.correct_answer: T' has vertices at (1,-1), (3,-1), (1,-3) — the correct rotation of T through 90° clockwise about O(0,0).
questions.mark_scheme: M1 for a triangle drawn with vertices consistent with a 90° rotation about O (clockwise or anticlockwise attempted, correct size and shape maintained). A1 for fully correct image T' with vertices at (1,-1), (3,-1), (1,-3), correctly labelled, in the correct clockwise sense (i.e. NOT the anticlockwise image which would have vertices at (-1,1), (-3,1), (-1,3)).
questions.misconception_targeted: Confusing clockwise and anticlockwise rotation direction

questions.correct_answer: Image S' has vertices at (-2,2), (-2,4), (0,4), (0,3), (-1,3), (-1,2) — i.e. shape S translated 3 units right and 2 units down, correctly plotted and labelled S'.
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for evidence of translating all vertices of S by +3 in the x-direction (regardless of y-direction error)
M1 for evidence of translating all vertices of S by -2 in the y-direction (regardless of x-direction error)
A1 for fully correct image drawn in the correct position (vertices at (-2,2), (-2,4), (0,4), (0,3), (-1,3), (-1,2)) and labelled S'

Note: a common error is swapping the components, translating by (-2, 3) instead of (3, -2) — award at most M1 if this error is made consistently, since only one of the two translation directions would be correct depending on interpretation.
questions.misconception_targeted: Swapping x and y components of the vector

questions.topic_aspect: Describing a single transformation fully (type, and required details) — rotation
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for identifying the transformation as a rotation (must not also mention reflection/translation/enlargement as alternatives)
A1 for correct angle and direction — $180^\circ$ (direction not required for $180^\circ$, but angle must be stated correctly, e.g. "half turn" or "$180^\circ$")
A1 for correct centre of rotation stated as $(0,0)$ (or origin)

Note: full marks only awarded if ALL THREE details (type, angle, centre) are correctly and unambiguously stated. Stating "rotation" alone scores M1 only; stating "rotation, $180^\circ$" without a centre scores M1A1 only (2 marks).
questions.misconception_targeted: Omitting key details e.g. not stating centre of rotation or scale factor

questions.topic_aspect: Enlargement with a positive integer scale factor from a centre of enlargement
questions.correct_answer: Image $T'$ has vertices at $(2,4)$, $(2,8)$ and $(6,4)$ (i.e. shape $T$ enlarged by scale factor 2 from centre $(-6,-2)$).
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for identifying the centre of enlargement $C=(-6,-2)$ and finding the vector from $C$ to at least one vertex of $T$ (e.g. $C$ to $A(-4,1)$ is $(2,3)$).
M1 for doubling the distance from $C$ to each vertex to find at least two correct new vertices (e.g. $A'=(-6,-2)+2(2,3)=(-2,4)$; correct new vertices are $A'=(-2,4)$, $B'=(-2,8)$, $D'=(2,4)$).
A1 for fully correct enlarged triangle $T'$ drawn with vertices at $(-2,4)$, $(-2,8)$, $(2,4)$, each side parallel to and twice the length of the corresponding side of $T$, with correct orientation relative to $C$.
Note: Award 0 for M1 if student only doubles the side lengths of $T$ in place without scaling distances from $C$ (common misconception).
questions.misconception_targeted: Not scaling distances from the centre correctly, only resizing shape in place

questions.topic_aspect: Enlargement with fractional and negative scale factors
questions.correct_answer:
(a) $T_1$ has vertices $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$ — a smaller triangle between the centre and the original, in the same orientation.
(b) $T_2$ has vertices $(-2,-2)$, $(-2,-4)$, $(-4,-2)$ — same size as $T$ but rotated $180^\circ$ (on the opposite side of $O$).
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) M1 for at least two vertices of $T_1$ correctly plotted (or correct coordinates stated) using scale factor $\tfrac{1}{2}$ from centre $(0,0)$, i.e. each coordinate of $A$, $B$, $C$ halved; A1 for fully correct triangle $T_1$ with vertices $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, correctly positioned between $O$ and $T$ (not enlarged, not on wrong side).

(b) M1 for at least two vertices of $T_2$ correctly plotted (or correct coordinates stated) using scale factor $-1$ from centre $(0,0)$, i.e. each coordinate of $A$, $B$, $C$ negated; A1 for fully correct triangle $T_2$ with vertices $(-2,-2)$, $(-2,-4)$, $(-4,-2)$, same size as $T$, on the opposite side of $O$ (180° rotated position), not on the same side as $T$.

Award 0 for M1 if scale factor $\tfrac{1}{2}$ is applied as if it enlarges (vertices doubled instead of halved) in part (a), or if scale factor $-1$ image is drawn on the same side as $T$ (just reflected in place) in part (b) — these indicate the targeted misconceptions.
questions.misconception_targeted: Believing fractional scale factor enlarges the shape, or misplacing image with negative scale factor on wrong side of centre

questions.topic_aspect: Similar shapes — finding an unknown side length using scale factor and ratios
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for identifying correct corresponding sides AB and DE (i.e. $17.5 \div 7$) to find the scale factor
M1 for correct scale factor $= 2.5$ (accept equivalent method using $EF \div BC = 13 \div 5.2 = 2.5$ as a check/alternative)
A1 for $DF = 6 \times 2.5 = 15$ cm

(If candidate incorrectly uses BC and EF as corresponding to AC, giving scale factor from wrong pair, award at most M1 for a consistent but incorrect method; full marks require correct correspondence $AB \leftrightarrow DE$, $BC \leftrightarrow EF$, $AC \leftrightarrow DF$.)
questions.misconception_targeted: Using the scale factor from the wrong pair of corresponding sides

questions.topic_aspect: Similar shapes — proving similarity and forming/solving an algebraic ratio equation for an unknown side
questions.correct_answer: (a) Triangles PQR and STR are similar (AA: shared angle at R, both have a right angle at Q and T since PQ and ST are vertical and QR is horizontal). (b) x = 9.5
questions.mark_scheme:
(a)
M1 for identifying angle R is common to both triangles (shared/vertically opposite angle)
A1 for identifying that angle PQR = angle STR = 90° (both PQ and ST are vertical, perpendicular to the horizontal ground QR), and concluding triangles are similar by AA (two pairs of equal angles)

(b)
QR = QT + TR = 5.4 + 4.8 = 10.2 m
M1 for setting up correct ratio equation using corresponding sides, e.g. (x+2)/3 = QR/TR = 10.2/4.8
M1 for correct rearrangement: x + 2 = 3 × (10.2/4.8) = 3 × 2.125 = 6.375... 

[Recompute cleanly: ratio = QR/TR = 10.2/4.8 = 2.125
x + 2 = 3 × 2.125 = 6.375
x = 4.375]

Note: mark scheme accepts equivalent correct method using QT and TR ratio consistently; final numerical answer confirmed as x = 4.375 (accept awrt 4.38)

A1 for correct equation: (x+2)/3 = 10.2/4.8
A1 for x = 4.375 (accept 4.38 or exact fraction 35/8)
questions.misconception_targeted: Assuming shapes are similar without checking angle or ratio conditions; incorrect algebraic setup of the ratio equation
